intro.sub: Candy Heist: DJ, producer and sound engineer. Kerala-born, Halifax-based, tuned in since 2018.

who.label: Who is Candy Heist

body.text: Somewhere between tech house bounce and dubstep intensity, Candy Heist
. Every set is part ritual, part signal, tuned to give back something the crowd didn’t know it had lost.

who.secondary: Off the decks he is a producer and sound engineer, which is why every Candy Heist set is built from the ground up.

photo.alt: Candy Heist at the decks beneath the vaulted, crimson-lit ceiling of a gothic hall

nayara.label: The world of Nayara
nayara.body: Nayara is the world Candy Heist built: a living planet that has forgotten what it once was, and a rogue sonoalchemist who uses sound to make it remember. It is the story his music tells. Every part of it stands in for something real, moments from his own life told in symbols.

behind.label: Behind the signal
behind.headline: The music is built, not just played.

paragraphs.text: Every Candy Heist track is taken apart before it ever reaches a room. As DJ, producer and sound engineer, he carries it from the first idea to the final master, then plays it out himself. The ears that read the crowd are the same ones that shaped the sound.
Between tech house bounce and dubstep intensity, each track is
: something the room forgot, rebuilt until it hits again. The groove is designed before it is played. The weight is engineered before it is felt.

roles.title: DJ
roles.body: Reading a room in real time: when to hold the groove, when to break it, and how long to make a crowd wait for the drop.

roles.title: Producer
roles.body: Building a track from nothing: the idea, the sound design and the arrangement, until the record carries the feeling it started with.

note.text: On record: 4x4, a four-track EP that includes Menace; Over The Moon, a SoundCloud exclusive; and the title track of G.Roy’s Truths Collide.

photo.alt: Candy Heist at the decks in front of a glowing spiral backdrop

roles.title: Sound engineer
roles.body: Making it land the way it was heard: the mix, the master, and a low end that holds its weight on any system.

continues.label: The signal continues
continues.headline: The frequency is still changing.
continues.lede: The sets, the records and the sessions are all still moving. Here is where the signal stands now.
